tasks.short: Confirm a patient's identity before the draw.

steps.what: Read the draw card before this check.
Confirm the identities of patients by verifying their personal information.
outputs: whether this is the right patient

tasks.design: A lab colleague writes a paper draw card with the patient name, the bay name, and the draw title. The phlebotomist reads it and confirms the patient's identity in person. The card does not hold the date of birth or the address.
tasks.previous_blocker: The draw list sat apart from the bay, so the search before the check was slow.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card names the bay. The identity check stays as it is.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this is the right patient still depends on the person in the chair.
tasks.human_edge: Only the phlebotomist can judge that the person matches the draw.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the bay. The phlebotomist still confirms the patient's identity.

reach.task: Confirm one patient's identity before care.
reach.learn: The card names the bay. The assistant still confirms the person.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the patient name, the bay name, and the draw title shortens the search. The phlebotomist still confirms the identity. Model knowledge of this design.

assumptions: The workplace is a mid-size European blood-draw room.
A lab colleague writes the draw card before the check.
Fields are the patient name, the bay name, and the draw title.
The draw card does not hold the date of birth or the address.
The phlebotomist confirms the identity at full time.
The check stays with the phlebotomist. There is no written note from this step.
If the row is missing, the phlebotomist reads the paper draw list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a lab colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
Staff consent for a monitoring or recording tool is out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this room already keeps a one-line card for each patient.
research_questions: How often the draw card has no row on the first check.

incremental.description: No extra phlebotomist upkeep. A lab colleague keeps the card.
A lab colleague writes the draw card: patient name, bay name, and draw title.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The check is the first one, so the draw card has no row and the phlebotomist reads the paper draw list. The search saving disappears.

steps.what: Read the entry card before this typing.

tasks.human_edge: Only the phlebotomist can judge which values are present and type them.

tasks.short: Write the route a specimen took.

steps.what: Read the specimen card before this route.
Carry the specimen from the chair to the laboratory bench.
Document route of specimens from collection to laboratory analysis and diagnosis.

tasks.design: A lab colleague writes a paper specimen card with the specimen name, the lab name, and the route title. The phlebotomist reads it, carries the specimen, and writes the route by hand. The card does not hold who held it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lab name sat apart from the specimen, so the search before the route was slow.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card names the lab. The carry and the written route stay as they are.
tasks.still_hard: Who held the specimen still depends on the walk from the chair to the bench.
tasks.human_edge: Only the phlebotomist can judge the route and write it down.
tasks.altitude: A card shortens finding the lab. The phlebotomist still carries the specimen and writes the route.

reach.task: Write the route one specimen took.
reach.learn: The card names the lab. The aide still carries the item and writes the route.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the specimen name, the lab name, and the route title shortens the search. The phlebotomist still carries the specimen and writes the route. Model knowledge of this design.

assumptions: The workplace is a mid-size European blood-draw room.
A lab colleague writes the specimen card before the route.
Fields are the specimen name, the lab name, and the route title.
The specimen card does not hold who held the specimen.
The phlebotomist carries the specimen and writes the route at full time.
The written specimen route is the phlebotomist's own writing. It is not posted anywhere else.
If the row is missing, the phlebotomist reads the paper lab list inside s1.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because a lab colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.

role.altitude: The phlebotomist still confirms identity, still types the specimen line, still tells the physician the result, and still writes the specimen route. A card only shortens finding the bay, the screen, the physician, or the lab.
reach: Nursing Assistants: confirm one patient after the card names the bay.
Medical Assistants: type one specimen line after the card names the screen.
Physical Therapist Assistants: tell one result after the card names the physician.
Pharmacy Aides: write one specimen route after the card names the lab.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper draw list when the card has no row.
Confirm the patient, the values, the result, and the route from the person and the specimen, not from the card.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not confirm a patient, type a specimen line, tell a physician, or write a route. The phlebotomist still does.
